experiment: E5 — matched-budget teacher-prefix continuation (C) vs student-prefix on-policy KD plus teacher recovery continuation (R)
status: REGISTERED — arm C built; bundle-atomic pairing, token targeting, KD-normalization proof and arm-R construction/gates complete; generation driver and full-path pilot next

treatment_description.R: student-prefix on-policy KD plus teacher recovery continuation
treatment_description.why_this_wording: kd_scope stays 'all' in both arms to preserve P2 objective semantics. In R that applies KD over the student-generated prefix states as well as the teacher recovery continuation, while CE is limited to the continuation. R therefore jointly tests learning on student-visited states AND teacher-guided recovery from those states.
forbidden_claims: describing R as pure continuation-only recovery
attributing an R result exclusively to the recovery continuation

symmetry_contract.shape: both arms are prefix + supervised continuation; C's prefix is teacher-native, R's is student-generated
symmetry_contract.prefix_length_matching: matched on truncation FRACTION by construction — paired C and R examples share seed material so they cut at the same relative depth. Absolute prefix tokens cannot match (teacher targets average 641 supervised tokens while student rollouts run far longer); the residual difference is measured and reported, never assumed away.
symmetry_contract.intended_sole_difference: the prefix state distribution: teacher-native (C) vs student-visited (R)

truncation_policy.deterministic: cut points are a pure function of the sample's identity hash; no global RNG, so a rebuild reproduces the corpus exactly
guards: continuation >= 8 tokens, so no cut at or past the answer end
prefix never ends on a stop token (no cut after a terminal answer)
the two truncations of one rollout are never identical
prefix and continuation lengths recorded per example
samples exceeding the context budget rejected deterministically before packing
packing never truncates a prefix or a supervised continuation

recovery_generation_gates: teacher received the exact serialized prompt and student prefix
teacher did not rewrite or omit the supplied prefix
continuation is non-empty and naturally terminated
no generation-time truncation or context-limit completion accepted
sample survives serialization and loader round-trip
supervised-token count exactly matches the loss mask
duplicate recovery targets measured and controlled
teacher answer internally valid under the task's verifier where one exists
rejection reasons and acceptance rates recorded by task and source seed

interpretation_boundaries.recipe_not_prefix_comparison: C/R vs the from-scratch P2-1.60M checkpoint differs in continuation schedule and data order, so it is a recipe comparison, not a pure prefix-distribution comparison
interpretation_boundaries.on_policy_source: per-seed recovery data generated by the corresponding P2-0.86M checkpoint is intentional; source checkpoint identity is stored on every sample
interpretation_boundaries.promotion_bar: a result must not be promoted on improved usable rollout alone; the question is whether student-prefix training converts more prompts into correct AND naturally terminated trajectories

budget_target.note: steps and packed blocks are matched between C and R; the 492/735,603 figures are the nested-rung origin of the budget, not a constraint on the split corpora

leakage_verified_offline.evaluation_battery: 150 prompts, mask d6e24e0b09da1bcc…, pinned to rung 860000

limitations: the evaluation battery is 150 shared TRAINING prompts — recall-style autonomous behaviour, not held-out generalization
one truncation policy and 100% recovery; a null means 'not under this policy and budget', not 'student-prefix recovery does not work'
n=2 seeds; every spread is one draw
teacher recovery targets inherit corpus v2's limitation that correctness is computed but not enforced (openmath targets ~38% correct)

paired_construction.requirement: the formal corpora are the PAIRED ACCEPTANCE INTERSECTION
paired_construction.rule: an R example failing generation or any quality gate removes the C example with the same (source_session_id, source_seed, truncation_index). Final C and R prompt/truncation composition is identical by construction, asserted before packing.
paired_construction.down_selection: deterministic largest-remainder allocation over strata of (task, source seed, truncation index, prefix-length bucket) — never the first N examples or blocks. Round-robin was implemented first and rejected: it over-represents small strata, measured at 6.7 pp drift on a 240-example synthetic corpus.
paired_construction.never_truncate_to_fit: whole paired samples are dropped in stratum order; no prefix or supervised continuation is ever cut to meet a budget

supervised_token_tolerance.definition: |C_supervised - R_supervised| / mean(C,R) <= 0.05, computed on supervised CONTINUATION tokens after paired selection
supervised_token_tolerance.registered_before: any R generation, training or evaluation
supervised_token_tolerance.why_a_tolerance_is_needed: exact equality is unreachable while keeping whole untruncated paired samples: C and R continuations differ in length because the underlying trajectories differ, and the only way to force equality would be to cut samples, which the registration forbids
supervised_token_tolerance.if_exceeded: STOP and report before training; do not adjust the tolerance

state_distribution_scope.matched: relative cut depth (truncation fraction), by construction
state_distribution_scope.claim_boundary: E5 tests the FULL student-visited state distribution. It does NOT isolate erroneous content alone: a student prefix differs from a teacher prefix in content, correctness, absolute length and context position simultaneously, and any effect may come from any of these.
state_distribution_scope.reporting: both relative cut fractions and absolute token-length distributions are reported for both arms

empty_prefix_exclusion.rule: k >= 1 always; a rollout that generated nothing is rejected
empty_prefix_exclusion.rationale: an empty student prefix collapses into ordinary teacher-prefix continuation and would not test student-prefix recovery
empty_prefix_exclusion.consequence: E5 therefore does NOT evaluate recovery from empty-output failures — the failure mode scaling repaired most often (50 of 88 repairs in the E4 transition table). The rejection census reports the cost by task and source seed.

pilot_gate.constraint: must use the same production code paths and schemas as the full run; a pilot that exercises a different path proves nothing
pilot_gate.on_failure: STOP before full generation and report

census_reconciliation.issue: the first arm-C build reported 2,292 accepted of 2,294 candidates with one rejection recorded — a gap of 2 explained by 1 rejection
census_reconciliation.cause: unit mismatch in reporting: rejections were counted per SESSION while the denominator counted EXAMPLES, and one rejected session removes two candidate examples. No sample was lost unexplained.
census_reconciliation.underlying_defect: the single rejection was a ~1-in-10,000 hash collision in the truncation-fraction draw. build_splits had an integer fallback for post-clamp collisions but it was unreachable for outright fraction collisions.
census_reconciliation.resolution: fallback wired for fraction collisions; arm C now builds at 2,294 of 2,294 = 100.0%. Censuses now report session-level and example-level counts separately.

token_accounting.principle: '492 blocks / 738 steps' is a COMPUTE budget and is NOT a definition of matched token scale. The registered scale target is the nested-rung increment of 735,603 supervised tokens, and both must be reported.
quantities_reported_for_each_packed_arm: unique supervised tokens (union per source trajectory)
final per-pass supervised continuation tokens (= CE-mask tokens)
total supervised-token presentations across 738 steps (= per-pass x passes)
KD-mask token count (kd_scope=all -> every non-padding token)
final comparison with the 735,603 nested-rung increment

suffix_overlap_measured_on_arm_C_sa.explanation: two cuts k1<k2 of one trajectory give nested continuations [k1,end) and [k2,end); the shorter is contained in the longer, so a naive sum double-counts it

feasibility_measured_before_spend.verdict: NO trade-off is required: the full candidate corpus occupies 63% of the 492-block budget, so the token target and the compute budget can both be met. The registered contingency (choose token-matched OR compute-matched) does not trigger.
feasibility_measured_before_spend.consequence: selecting down to the 735,603 target lowers utilisation further and adds padding, which the maintainer explicitly accepted in preference to missing the token scale

token_accounting.tolerance_is_a_ceiling: the 5% C/R bound is a hard stop, not an aim; the selector minimises the worse arm's deviation from the target subject to whole untruncated samples
token_accounting.forbidden_phrasing: a compute-matched 492-block/738-step continuation must NOT be called '1.60M-equivalent' in token scale

atomic_bundles.rule: a bundle survives only if every truncation passes generation and all ten gates in R; if either fails, both truncations are removed from both C and R
atomic_bundles.selection_unit: the two-truncation bundle is the smallest selectable unit for token-target selection and stratified down-selection
atomic_bundles.why: allowing a session to contribute one surviving cut would silently change the registered two-truncations-per-prompt design for part of the corpus
atomic_bundles.implementation: paired_corpus.intersect / take_bundles / select_paired, asserted by tests including a single-cut-survivor case

kd_normalization_verified.verified_through: the real Trainer.step_once, not a reimplementation
kd_normalization_verified.result: PASS — prefix length does not alter the effective CE/KD weighting
properties_proven: CE is normalized only over CE-mask continuation tokens
KD is normalized only over KD-mask (non-padding) prediction positions
KD is not summed without normalization
KD is not divided by block length
KD is not divided by the CE denominator
ce_weight and kd_weight remain the effective coefficients in both arms
kd_normalization_verified.interpretation: both terms are per-token MEANS, so a longer prefix changes the CE denominator but not the KD denominator and does not reweight KD against CE. What a longer prefix does change is KD's COMPOSITION — 4.18 vs 9.44 KD tokens per CE token — which is the E5 treatment, not an implementation artifact.

token_target_terminology.the_target: ~735,603 refers to CE-MASK SUPERVISED-TOKEN INSTANCES PER PASS, not unique trajectory tokens
token_target_terminology.forbidden: describing the result as 735,603 unique recovery tokens
report_separately: unique supervised coverage by original trajectory
total CE-token presentations across the three passes

feasibility_status.status: NOT YET JOINTLY SATISFIED — C-only evidence is insufficient
feasibility_status.must_be_demonstrated_by: the production R corpus or a sufficiently representative production-path pilot
joint_conditions: ~735,603 CE-mask tokens per arm within the 5% tolerance
no truncation of any prefix or continuation
feasibility_status.hypothesis_not_fact: that R continuations will be longer than C's is a HYPOTHESIS until measured; the token-target selector makes no assumption about it and scores both arms

required: approximate fraction of total loss attributable to prefix KD
kd_signal_strength_on_real_student_prefi.why: normalization correctness says nothing about magnitude. The controlled measurement showed a weighted KD term of 0.0064 against a weighted CE term of 7.60 — under 0.1% of the loss. If prefix KD is a rounding error on real data too, R's treatment is weaker than its name suggests and the write-up must say so rather than describing student-visited-state learning as a major component.

the_pilot_proves: pipeline correctness end to end through production code
pilot_status_boundary.the_pilot_does_not_prove: that the complete corpus satisfies the joint token/block constraints
pilot_status_boundary.final_joint_feasibility: checked only after the COMPLETE R corpus is generated and paired with C
pilot_status_boundary.on_conflict: if the full corpus cannot simultaneously satisfy the CE-token target, atomic bundles, the 492-block budget and the C/R tolerance, STOP before training and report the measured conflict

gradient_attribution.correction_accepted: scalar loss share is NOT gradient share. CE and KL have different numerical scales, so a term with a tiny value can still steer the update.
required_on_real_C_and_R_pilot_batches: the same statistics by FFN / attention-projection / norm parameter group

method.why_shared_denominator: re-normalizing prefix-only KD over its own token count measures a different objective; sharing kd_total makes the pieces sum to the term the trainer optimizes

gradient_attribution.degenerate_teacher_refused: a teacher that is a copy of the student gives KL == 0 identically, which would render every KD number 0.0 and read as a finding. The tool refuses unless --allow-degenerate-teacher is passed explicitly.

interpretation_rule.if_loss_AND_gradient_both_negligible: describe R as primarily 'teacher recovery continuation CE conditioned on student-generated context, with a very small on-policy KD component'
interpretation_rule.if_scalar_small_but_gradient_material: do NOT call it a rounding error; report the gradient contribution as the operative quantity
